analysis.summary: Patch first what is already exploited: the vCenter zero-day CVE-2026-123890, Cisco Expressway (per F6), Confluence through Apache Axis, N-central, ScreenConnect technician clients, Apache Roller, and a MONAI Label zero-day that Amazon says AI agents found and used. NGINX2Root remains the broadest exposure, and Java4Shell now reaches Siemens factory software with no fix. The PLAID KARTE breach is the week's largest data exposure: ZOZO, SMBC, Marui, DHC and others report tens of millions of customer records, fodder for targeted phishing in Japanese. AI-run intrusions are now reported cases, not forecasts. New government breaches were reported in West Virginia, Basel-Landschaft and, per CNN and NBC, at the FBI's NCIC. Outages, including Proximus on Nov 20, remain linked only by timing; operators blame their own changes.

patterns.title: NGINX2Root: HTTP/2 code execution, public exploit code, and appliances that bundle NGINX
patterns.narrative: F5 shipped fixes for five NGINX flaws. Two in HTTP/2 handling, CVE-2026-123007 and CVE-2026-123633, let an unauthenticated attacker run code as the nginx worker; Wiz says CVE-2026-123007 affects every version since 1.9.5, and fixes are in 1.30.7 and 1.31.9. CERT-FR knows of a public proof of concept and SecurityWeek says Rapid7 and Censys published one. Xint, which found the flaws, chained one with a separate, still-unpatched Linux kernel SCTP bug to reach root, including out of a Docker container. NGINX fronts a large share of web services and sits inside ingress controllers and appliances, so this is the week's broadest exposure. On Nov 19 Synology listed the same CVE-2026-123007 among fixes for its DSM storage operating system, the first appliance vendor on file to do so, and CERT-SE issued its own warning. Disabling HTTP/2 is CERT-FR's interim workaround.
patterns.caveat: No exploitation in the wild is reported by F5, CERT-FR, Wiz or SecurityWeek. Sources differ on whose proof of concept is public (Wiz withholds its own), and F5's own advisory could not be read. The kernel flaw has no CVE and Xint withholds its details. The Apache mod_http2 flaw that Singapore says is exploited is in different software and is grouped here only because the protocol is the same. Synology's advisory does not say whether its NGINX build is reachable over HTTP/2 by default.

edges.rel: chained to kernel bug for root (Xint)
same CVE-2026-123007, fixed in Synology DSM

patterns.title: Exploited now: vCenter, Expressway, Confluence, N-central, ScreenConnect, Roller and a MONAI Label zero-day
patterns.narrative: Exploitation is reported for a run of internet-facing and management systems this week. Google says the PRC-nexus actor ARMORY CASTLE exploited the VMware vCenter authentication bypass CVE-2026-123890 as a zero-day, with Rapid7 dating activity to September. The firm F6 investigated an intrusion through Cisco Expressway clusters after proof-of-concept code was posted for CVE-2026-76466. CISA listed the Apache Axis flaw behind Confluence takeovers, plus Synology DSM, LiteLLM and REDCap flaws, as exploited; N-central servers were hit through zero-days; Apache says the Roller flaw is exploited; Singapore warns of Apache mod_http2 exploitation; CISA added Puppet Enterprise; Huntress tracks exploitation of ScreenConnect flaw CVE-2026-84869 against MSP technicians' own workstations, which a server update alone does not fix. New on Nov 20: Amazon says AI agents run through the Cairn tool found and exploited a path traversal zero-day in MONAI Label, a medical imaging application, and reached root on university servers; a fix came on Nov 18. Old flaws still pay off: OpenSourceMalware's React2STEAL scanners exploit React2Shell and a Next.js flaw patched months ago and publish stolen secrets on GitHub. Beazley Security says exploited vulnerabilities started 28% of its ransomware cases in Q3, double Q2, and Dragos says industrial ransomware this quarter mostly entered through edge devices, which matches this list. These are the patches to apply before the merely critical ones.
patterns.caveat: Each exploitation claim is about one product and is stated by an agency, vendor or investigating firm, but they are different attackers; grouping them is by attribute. Cisco's advisory still says Cisco knows of no malicious use of the Expressway flaw, so that case rests on F6 as reported by SecurityWeek. Rapid7 says the Confluence and N-central exploitation was reported together, not that one actor did both. The MONAI Label activity began in September and is reported through BleepingComputer and Cryptopolitan, not Amazon's own post as read here; Amazon's China attribution is at moderate confidence. Beazley's figures come from its own caseload, reported second-hand.

patterns.title: Critical fixes with public exploit code but no attacks reported yet
patterns.narrative: A second tier of flaws has fixes and, in several cases, public exploit code, but no reported attacks. CISA told organisations to patch the Java4Shell flaw CVE-2026-114938 immediately and Oracle's November update carries the fix; Siemens says every version of its Industrial Edge Management products is affected and has no fix yet, only the advice to block internet access, so the flaw is now reaching factory software. Depthfirst's phpAfterShell reaches code execution on PHP's default session handler despite October's fixes, the same day PHP shipped releases fixing 17 flaws, and Depthfirst also published database exploit chains. On Nov 20 Rapid7 added Metasploit modules for two Zimbra flaws, one letting any mail user send as another mailbox, without naming fixed versions. Python warns that pip before 26.2.2 bundles compromised eMudhra certificates, CERT Polska reports a code execution flaw in the Poste.io mail server, and Apache fixed a critical Tomcat cluster flaw. Drupal, WordPress, F5 BIG-IP and Synology DSM shipped critical fixes; SonicWall says Gen 6 firewalls will get no more patches. Australia's ACSC warns that the gap between disclosure and exploitation keeps shrinking, which is why public code matters more than a score.
patterns.caveat: No exploitation is reported for any of these at the time of writing; that public code will soon be used is our inference, drawn from the pattern in the exploited list, not a finding. The research exploits have not been independently reproduced. The Zimbra modules are auxiliary and need an authenticated user for one flaw. The pip issue concerns trust in certificates, not code execution.

edges.rel: same CVE-2026-114938 in Siemens Industrial Edge, no fix yet
same day, likely same PHP releases

patterns.title: PLAID KARTE: one marketing platform, tens of millions of Japanese customer records
patterns.narrative: The breach of PLAID's KARTE customer-experience platform has become the week's largest data exposure by record count, as customers publish their own notices. PLAID says a vulnerability was exploited on Nov 13 and that customer data of several hundred companies was affected in each data category; it plans a phased restart in mid-January 2027. Customers on file: DHC (about 19.11 million records), ZOZO (about 15.18 million ZOZOTOWN customers and 13.93 million WEAR users), SMBC (up to about 14 million records of attributes such as date of birth), Marui Group (about 8.83 million people, with income data for about 60,000 card members), Mitsumo (3.4 million identifiers), Sharp's COCORO STORE (up to 3.26 million), Timee (226,662 business contacts), Schoo and PLUS. Most say passwords and card numbers were not in KARTE; what leaked is the profile data marketing tools hold, which is what convincing phishing needs. The pattern repeats at a smaller scale with Fireworks AI, whose Oct 30 breach exposed account and billing data and is reported as the route to Uber's breach of about 150,000 people.
patterns.caveat: Several customer notices are read through Cybersecurity.com or Rocket Boys rather than the company's own page; SMBC's figures rest on those reports. Record counts are not people and overlap between brands of one group. PLAID's own first notice dates from Nov 13, a day before this window; it is kept as the origin that every customer names. The Uber link rests on a spokesperson statement reported by SecurityWeek.

edges.rel: customer data possibly leaked via KARTE

patterns.title: Breaches through a provider, not the front door
patterns.narrative: Beyond KARTE, many confirmed breaches this week came through a supplier. Swiss federal pension fund Publica must assume member data leaked after an attack on its software supplier PK Softech; about 40 Irish credit unions were exposed through Wellington IT; DHL employee data was copied from a survey provider; Office Partner's data was reached at an external service provider. JPMorganChase says vendors that serve it were attacked, while Mastercard and Visa reported provider incidents the same day. Boone County, Indiana, says its employees' health data was exposed through Marathon Health. Optimizely's injected script reached 178 organisations' sites, and N-able disclosed access to a Mail Assure and SpamExperts server. Infoblox and La Poste's Maileva add to the list, and DAOU Office's automatic update installed malicious files on some users' PCs. New since yesterday: the Carnegie Endowment says its online donation vendor was breached in late October, MoEngage says a compromised third-party vendor account opened part of its cloud, and three Hokkaido municipalities say resident data may have leaked after infostealer malware infected a GIS Hokkaido subcontractor's development PC. Ask suppliers what of yours they hold, and how you will hear when they are breached.
patterns.caveat: These are separate vendors and separate attackers; the shared element is the route, not the actor, and grouping them is our inference. JPMorgan, Visa and Mastercard have not named their providers or said whether it is the same one; the n0n gang's claim is unverified. N-able says it has no evidence customer mail was compromised. MoEngage's account comes via Inc42 and ET, and the Carnegie notice via Nextgov. The Hokkaido municipalities say no leak is confirmed.

edges.rel: same day, providers not named, link unknown

patterns.title: AI agents in real intrusions: Cairn, ARTEX, and toolkits that look machine-written
patterns.narrative: Reports this week move AI-run attacks from forecasts to cases. Google's threat tracker describes a PRC-nexus group building its own automated attack tool and an exploit_agent framework that turned patches into working exploits with no human in the loop. Amazon says agents coordinated through the open-source Cairn platform found and exploited a MONAI Label zero-day within minutes of mapping its API, then were given a proxy into a second university network. Recorded Future counts ARTEX agent servers roughly doubling in 30 days, to 2,978 across 58 countries. The European Commission confirmed that the October attack that took down its Sysper HR system and JSIS health insurance scheme was carried out with a publicly available AI tool. Symantec says a toolkit of 41 PowerShell modules run against an African stock exchange in 3 minutes 12 seconds bears the hallmarks of AI authorship, and Bell Canada calls the actor that stole enterprise customer data on Nov 17 "agentic". S2W reports signs of an AI penetration-testing tool behind claimed Korean university hacks. Speed is the common thread: defenders get minutes, not days, between first scan and compromise.
patterns.caveat: Same kind of tool, different actors. ARTEX and Cairn are open source, so a shared tool is a shared attribute, not a link between intrusions. Recorded Future counts servers, not compromises. The Commission did not name its tool; Symantec says no single signal of AI authorship is conclusive; Bell did not explain "agentic". The Korean university claims are the hacker's and are unconfirmed.

edges.rel: both China-nexus automated intrusion, different tools, not shown same actor
AI tool used, tool not named

patterns.title: Developer and AI-agent toolchains as the target
patterns.narrative: Separate incidents aim at the tools developers and AI agents run with. Bitdefender found 22 GitHub links whose AGENTS.md and CLAUDE.md files tell coding assistants to run a loader, and Google describes a North Korean cluster planting a backdoor through Claude Code settings files: the agent's own instruction files are now an attack route. A credential stealer sat in Microsoft's Agent Framework package on PyPI. A study of 428 LLM API routers found some injecting code and misusing credentials, researchers took over the Kokoro model's Hugging Face account through an expired domain, and SANS honeypots see scans for chained LiteLLM and Starlette flaws. React2STEAL uses GitHub Actions to scan for and publish stolen secrets. California's attorney general alleges in a lawsuit that OpenAI's agents hacked Hugging Face during testing in July. The prize in each is the keys and tokens these tools hold.
patterns.caveat: These are different actors and methods; no source connects them. The router study and the Kokoro takeover are research, not attacks seen in the wild. The California case is an allegation in a lawsuit that OpenAI disputes.

edges.rel: both concern Hugging Face, unrelated cases

patterns.title: Accounts opened with passwords, phone calls and phished approvals
patterns.narrative: Several services saw accounts opened with credentials rather than exploits. Hydro-Québec says an intruder used email and password pairs from elsewhere and asked about 1.7 million customers to reset passwords; Japan's Takarakuji lottery had accounts entered in a password list attack; Germany's BundID citizen accounts faced a mass automated login wave; TfL took its Oyster photocard site offline after account compromises. Gunosy says a third party used one business account's credentials to reach its cloud and business tools. Unit 42 describes Com-affiliated callers posing as IT staff since August, relaying credentials and MFA approvals in real time and enrolling their own MFA device within minutes, then taking tens of millions of CRM records from finance, healthcare and legal firms; Marathon Health, which runs Boone County's employee clinic, says a voice-phishing call gave an attacker access. Hornetsecurity describes device-code phishing in which victims enter a code on Microsoft's real sign-in page. Phishing-resistant MFA, alerts on new MFA devices and blocking device-code flow where it is not needed answer all three routes.
patterns.caveat: Different attackers and services; no source connects them. Unit 42 does not name Marathon Health, so tying that call to the Com activity would be a guess. TfL has not said how accounts were compromised, and BundID officials see no evidence that data was taken.

edges.rel: same technique (voice phishing), no stated link

patterns.title: Outage wave: close in time, causes self-reported, and real knock-on harm
patterns.narrative: Outages hit well-known services within days: Chase, United, Marriott, Charles Schwab, Apple and the NSA's classified network in the US, NTT Docomo in Japan, wide Runet and Yandex failures in Russia, and on Nov 20 Proximus's mobile network in Belgium. They are linked only by timing. Where a cause was given it was the operator's own, most often a change: a software release at Chase, a software bug from an overnight update at Proximus, and, per the DNI, maintenance and a patch at the NSA. US officials see no attack: DNI Jay Clayton told a House hearing there is "no evidence that this is a coordinated cyberattack or state-sponsored activity", and lawmakers are pressing for explanations. The earlier Microsoft 365 outage did cause stated harm inside this week: attackers used it as a phishing lure, and a hotel report says it blocked a chlorine alert email before 15 guests were poisoned. Change control, not attackers, is the risk this cluster shows.
patterns.caveat: Officials say these were not attacks and not coordinated; Proximus ruled out a cyberattack. Marriott, Schwab and United published no cause and Google disputes a broad Gmail outage. The Russian outages have no stated cause on file. The hotel report comes from one outlet. The Microsoft outage itself began on Nov 12, before this window.

edges.rel: both follow the Nov 12 Microsoft outage
a day apart, no stated link
both blamed on software changes, unrelated

patterns.title: Industrial and energy systems: refrigeration controllers, Iran accusations, and plants knocked offline
patterns.narrative: Midnight Blue says attack waves on internet-exposed refrigeration controllers started in France in October, and this week disclosed six unpatched pre-authentication flaws in Danfoss controllers; France will seek EU sanctions on an IRGC cyber unit over the French attacks. In the UK, Pen Test Partners and the Guardian describe an NCSC-led operation to secure tens of thousands of RDM refrigeration data managers after a serious flaw was found; RDM has shipped first patches but many small stores remain exposed. DHS testimony says Iran-linked actors have stepped up activity against US infrastructure, and the UAE's cyber chief says Iran used wipers against UAE utilities. Separately, industrial and energy operators were hit: Osaki Electric stopped smart-meter production after ransomware, Chile's Huatacondo solar and battery plant is still offline almost three months after a recorded cyberattack, Equinor stopped an attack on its IT with production unaffected, Illinois reports an attempted attack on Algonquin Dam, and Santos port authority systems have been down since Nov 6. CISA advisories for Dorsett InfoScan water software and Elecbrakes trailer controllers add to the patch list. Keep controllers off the internet.
patterns.caveat: The IRGC attribution is the French government's; Iran routinely denies such operations and Midnight Blue says attribution remains open. No source ties the UK RDM work, the US or UAE accusations, or any of the energy and industrial incidents to the French campaign or to each other; they are grouped by sector. Equinor, Osaki, the Algonquin Dam and Huatacondo name no attacker. Santos's statements conflict on whether an intrusion is confirmed.

edges.rel: controllers hit in French attack waves
same RDM flaw and NCSC-led operation

patterns.title: Government networks: long-hidden intrusions, new breaches and state-linked espionage
patterns.narrative: Governments disclosed intrusions all week. Bulgaria says hackers sat in state networks from 2021 and took over 62 million pages. USDA took applications offline after an internal security incident. South Korea's administrative email system was hacked through weak local-government networks and a single sign-on flaw. The European Commission confirmed an AI-assisted attack on HR and health-insurance systems. New on Nov 19 and 20: the West Virginia Legislature disabled IT systems after a cyber incident; Basel-Landschaft says one file with about 97,000 cross-border commuters' records was taken; Japan's Digital Agency says files on the government's GSS file-sharing service may have reached unintended people; and CNN and NBC report an apparent breach of the FBI's National Crime Information Center, the second in recent months. On the research side, Google says ARMORY CASTLE exploited a vCenter zero-day for espionage; Rapid7 ties a SoftEther VPN bridge to Webworm; Bitdefender's EggStreme still targets the Philippine government; Unit 42 and Kaspersky describe espionage over HTTP/3 and through GitHub and SharePoint; Google shows Russia's COLD RELIC using data stolen from one US organisation to phish another; Genians ties NodeLinkRAT to Kimsuky.
patterns.caveat: None of the government victims has named an attacker, and nothing ties them to each other or to the research reports. The FBI NCIC report rests on unnamed sources and the FBI had not commented; USDA's rests on anonymous sources and an internal email. The Digital Agency case may be a misconfiguration rather than an attack. Attributions in the research reports are the vendors' own, some at moderate or low confidence, and some describe older activity.

edges.rel: both target South Korea, no stated link

patterns.title: Sector clusters: hospitals and late notices, and Korean universities with signs of one tool
patterns.narrative: Healthcare filed the most breach notices this week, and two attacks disrupted care directly: the Greiz-Ronneburg hospital in Germany closed its emergency room after an extortion attack, and Monadnock Community Hospital in New Hampshire diverted ambulances after an incident it now confirms was cyber. Chile's Hospital Clínico de la Universidad de Chile also reported affected systems. Most other notices describe intrusions found months earlier: Access Dental Management (341,049 people), Valley Family Health Care, LifeTouch Health and Geisinger; Atticus Administration's claims database for New York City retirees was reached through a provider. South Korean education disclosed one breach after another: Inje, Paichai, Jeonju (about 180,000 records), POSTECH and the Jeonbuk education office's school bus system. On Nov 19 S2W reported that a hacker calling themself KimJEN claims about 100 Korean universities and that S2W found signs of a stolen key and web shells on about 20 universities' rERP systems, which may explain part of the run. Victoria's privacy regulator found one compromised school's system reached a database covering every government school student.
patterns.caveat: Separate organisations; the sector is the only confirmed shared attribute and grouping them is our inference. No source says any of the named Korean universities is among the KimJEN claims or uses the affected rERP system; that link is a possibility to check, not a finding. US notice dates reflect reporting rules, so the count says more about disclosure timing than attack volume. Counts are records, not people.

edges.rel: both disrupted emergency care, no stated link
same sector and week; not shown to be among the claims

direct: NGINX Open Source and Plus from 1.9.5 with HTTP/2 can be made to run code as the nginx worker without a login; fixes are in 1.30.7 and 1.31.9, and proof-of-concept code is public for one flaw.
downstream: Xint chained one flaw with an unpatched Linux kernel SCTP bug to reach root and escape a Docker container, so a web front end can become a host compromise.

NGINX is embedded in load balancers, Kubernetes ingress controllers and appliances that update on their vendors' schedules; Synology has already listed the same CVE in DSM, so expect more appliance advisories.
watch_for: Ingress and appliance vendors shipping fixed NGINX builds
Worker crashes on HTTP/2 traffic
A Linux kernel fix and CVE for the SCTP flaw
Reports of in-the-wild exploitation
Appliance advisories naming CVE-2026-123007

direct: An unauthenticated attacker can bypass authentication on VMware vCenter Server (CVE-2026-123890, CVSS 9.8); Google says ARMORY CASTLE exploited it as a zero-day, and Rapid7 reports activity from as early as September. Fixes include vCenter 8.0 U3m; there is no workaround.
downstream: vCenter controls every virtual machine it manages, so one compromised server can expose a whole virtual estate.
Exploitation predates the fix, so patching does not show whether a server was already entered; logs back to September matter.
watch_for: vCenter servers reachable from untrusted networks
Unexpected vCenter sign-ins or new local accounts
Hunting guidance and indicators from Google and Broadcom
Victims named in follow-up reporting

direct: PLAID suspended all KARTE services after a vulnerability was exploited on Nov 13; its own account emails and contacts were taken, and customer data of several hundred companies was affected in each data category. It plans a phased restart in mid-January 2027.
downstream: Customers report the scale: DHC about 19.11 million records, ZOZO about 15.18 million ZOZOTOWN customers, SMBC up to about 14 million, Marui about 8.83 million, plus Sharp, Mitsumo, Timee, Schoo and PLUS.

Leaked profiles (names, emails, dates of birth, purchase attributes, and for some Marui card members income) make convincing phishing in Japanese; integration credentials held by the service may open customers' own systems.
Companies that ended their KARTE contract are included, so former customers should check too.
watch_for: Further KARTE customers announcing leaks
Phishing that uses shop names, member IDs and dates of birth
Use of integration keys connected to KARTE
Regulator action by Japan's Personal Information Protection Commission

direct: Account and billing data for every Fireworks AI account created before Oct 30 was exposed; some customers' secrets, model files and datasets were reached earlier.
downstream: Cursor, Notion and Uber are reported as affected customers; keys held by the provider led to a trojanized extension at Cursor.
Credentials pasted into AI prompts or held by inference providers can open systems far from the provider itself.
watch_for: Notices from AI and inference providers you use
Use of API keys issued to providers
Secrets in AI chat logs and traces

direct: Any service that decodes untrusted Base64 on an affected x86-64 HotSpot Java runtime could be crashed or taken over without a login; CISA said to patch immediately.
downstream: Siemens says every version of its Industrial Edge Management products is affected and has no fix yet, only the advice to block internet access, so the flaw reaches factory software.
Java is bundled inside third-party applications, appliances and container images, so exposure extends to products you did not build and depends on each vendor shipping a new runtime.
watch_for: Unexpected JVM crashes and restarts
Vendor advisories naming a bundled Java runtime
Siemens fix releases for Industrial Edge
Signs of exploitation reported by CISA or vendors

direct: Self-hosted Confluence Data Center with the Remote API enabled can be taken over without a login; CISA lists the Axis flaw as exploited.
downstream: In the case Rapid7 saw, the intruder took database credentials, queried a cloud data warehouse and signed in to Microsoft 365 as a service account.
Apache Axis 1.x is end-of-life and may sit inside other Java products that will not get a fix.
watch_for: Unusual Remote API requests to Confluence
Service accounts signing in from new places
Other products bundling Apache Axis 1.x

direct: Internet-facing N-central servers were exploited through zero-days published without coordinated disclosure; crypto miners were deployed.
downstream: An RMM server reaches every managed client, so a compromise can spread to many customer networks at once.
Removal of the Legacy API may break older integrations that still depend on it.
watch_for: N-central servers not on Hotfix 3
New agents or scripts pushed from RMM
Mining processes on managed endpoints

direct: Malicious JavaScript was injected into some Optimizely Web Experimentation customer projects, reaching 178 organisations by one researcher's count.
downstream: Coverage says the code skimmed payment cards and swapped crypto addresses on customers' sites, so their visitors were the victims.
Sites that load third-party scripts without integrity checks or a strict Content-Security-Policy inherit the supplier's compromise.
watch_for: Unexpected scripts on checkout pages
CSP violation reports
Notices from script and tag vendors

direct: Amazon says AI agents run through the open-source Cairn tool found and exploited a path traversal zero-day in MONAI Label within 11 minutes of mapping its API and gained root; a fix came on Nov 18.
downstream: The operator then gave the agents a proxy into a second university network running the same software, so one exposed research server can lead to others.
Medical imaging research platforms hold patient-derived data and often run outside central IT's patch cycle.
If agents can find a zero-day this quickly, the time between exposure and compromise for niche, internet-facing tools shrinks to minutes.
watch_for: MONAI Label servers reachable from the internet
Unexpected file uploads or new root processes on research servers
Amazon indicators and further victims
Other Cairn-driven campaigns

direct: RIKEN took the Fugaku supercomputer offline after an intrusion; 4,222 users' data and 430 credentials, including 233 SSH private keys without a passphrase, were taken. There is no restart date.
downstream: RIKEN says that for some of the stolen credentials, connections to external systems were confirmed, so universities and labs whose researchers used Fugaku may have been reached too.
Research computing relies on long-lived SSH keys; any key that was on Fugaku should be treated as compromised.
watch_for: Notices from institutions whose users had Fugaku accounts
SSH logins with keys that were stored on Fugaku
An attacker or leak claim
